title: Canonical local charts of a positive finite-algebra quotient
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings with $S$ a finite $R$-algebra [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $p$ be a prime ideal of $R$. Put $A=R_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $B=A\otimes_R S$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $J=pB$, and $Q=\{q\subset S:q\text{ is prime and }q\cap R=p\}$. Choose $S$-algebra maps $\psi_q:B\to S_q$ and an integer $n\ge1$. Set $K_q=\operatorname{map}(\psi_q,J)$ and $C=B/J^n$. There is an index equivalence $e:Q\simeq\operatorname{MaxSpec}(C)$ characterized by contraction of $e(q)$ along $S\to B\to C$ being $q$. For each $q$, the ring $S_q/K_q^n$, as a $C$-algebra via the induced quotient map, is a localization of $C$ at the complement of $e(q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Here $\operatorname{MaxSpec}(C)$ is the type of maximal ideals of $C$; quotient means the usual ideal quotient, and extension is the ideal generated by the images.

source.place: Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension), the prime correspondence for n >= 1; Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization) and Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient)

proof.text: Use IsLocalization.tensorRight to realize B as the localization of S at the image M of R minus p. For each prime q over p, disjoint_primeCompl_of_liesOver, isPrime_of_isPrime_disjoint and under_map_of_isPrime_disjoint give its prime extension P and contraction P back to q. Since J is contained in P, so is J^n. Map P through the quotient map pi to define e0(q). Conversely, contract a maximal ideal of B/J^n to a prime P of B. Ideal.IsPrime.le_of_pow_le gives J contained in P. Contract to S; its contraction to R contains p, and a base element outside p is a unit in B, so cannot lie in P. Thus this contraction is a prime over p. Localization extension-contraction and quotient extension-contraction give the two inverse identities, hence Equiv.ofBijective e0 and the required contraction formula.

Every prime P of B containing J contracts to a prime of A containing pA, which is the maximal ideal of A. Hence its contraction is exactly this maximal ideal. The finite A-algebra B is integral. Apply Ideal.isMaximal_of_isIntegral_of_isMaximal_comap, the maximal-ideal consequence of integral incomparability, to show P maximal. Its quotient image is maximal by Ideal.IsMaximal.map_of_surjective_of_ker_le. No discrete-spectrum theorem or Noetherian hypothesis is used.

For fixed q give T=S_q its B-algebra structure through psi(q). The S-algebra compatibility gives a scalar tower. Since M is contained in the complement of q, isLocalization_of_submonoid_le makes T the localization of B at the image of that complement. The contraction of the maximal ideal of T to B is P: both ideals contract to q in S, and localization contraction is injective. Therefore all elements outside P map to units in T. IsLocalization.of_le enlarges the denominators to the complement of P. Apply IsLocalization.of_surjective to pi:B->B/J^n and T->T/K^n. The compatibility square is the defining quotientMap identity, and the kernel condition is Ideal.map_pow. Finally map_primeCompl_comap_of_surjective identifies the image of the complement of P with the complement of e(q), since the quotient contraction of e(q) is P. This proves the precise IsLocalization.AtPrime predicate for the stated quotientMap algebra structure. The construction and inverse maps require no nonempty assumption and cover empty fibres.

proof_origin.place: Tags 07N9, 00E3, 00CT; D4 Lean proof uses direct integral maximality (Mathlib Ideal.isMaximal_of_isIntegral_of_isMaximal_comap) instead of the finite discrete-spectrum detour.

lean.statement:
theorem localized_finite_quotient_charts
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.Finite R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    let A := Localization.AtPrime p
    let B := A ⊗[R] S
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := R) (A := A) (B := S)
    let J := p.map (algebraMap R B)
    let Q := p.primesOver S
    ∀ (ψ : ∀ q : Q, B →ₐ[S] Localization.AtPrime q.1) (n : ℕ), n ≠ 0 →
      let K := fun q : Q ↦ J.map (ψ q).toRingHom
      ∃ e : Q ≃ MaximalSpectrum (B ⧸ J ^ n),
        (∀ q : Q, (e q).asIdeal.comap
          ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ n)).comp (algebraMap S B)) = q.1) ∧
        ∀ q : Q,
          let f : (B ⧸ J ^ n) →+* (Localization.AtPrime q.1 ⧸ (K q) ^ n) :=
            Ideal.quotientMap ((K q) ^ n) (ψ q).toRingHom (by
            rw [← Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap, Ideal.map_pow])
          letI := f.toAlgebra
          IsLocalization.AtPrime (Localization.AtPrime q.1 ⧸ (K q) ^ n) (e q).asIdeal
